“Company Adverse Change” means any event or situation that has, or would reasonably be expected to have, a material adverse impact on (i) the business, assets, or financial condition of the Company and its Subsidiaries, or (ii) the capability of the Company to consummate the contemplated transactions. However, no such exclusion shall apply if such events, individually or in the aggregate, result in a disproportionate adverse effect relative to similar companies operating in the same industry.

Notably, the ability to consummate is only impacted by the conditions of (ii) if they do not fall under any of the exclusions set forth for Company Adverse Change.

In light of the identical treatment of the consummation ability in the exclusion clauses and the MAE definition, the text contends that the ability to consummate is functionally immune to the carveouts.
